bootstrap.generator: Python random.Random, Mersenne Twister, using choices with equal weights
bootstrap.row_order: Eligible participant rows in the processed CSV order, identified by the input hash
bootstrap.unit: One complete participant row; all measures use the same sampled rows in each replicate
bootstrap.draw_rule: Resample n complete participant rows with replacement
bootstrap.standard_error: Sample standard deviation of the bootstrap means, denominator B - 1
bootstrap.exact_empirical_standard_error: Analytic SE times sqrt((n - 1) / n), for the empirical distribution with replacement
bootstrap.percentile_interval: Percentile interval with linear interpolation at the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles
bootstrap.finite_replicates: SE and percentile estimates have Monte Carlo variation from the finite number of replicates.
bootstrap.replicate_alignment: Element i in both bootstrap_means arrays comes from the same participant draw.

interpretation.sample_sd: Spread of individual participants' measurements in the original units
interpretation.mean_offset: For an arithmetic mean, the empirical-bootstrap expectation equals the observed mean. The reported bootstrap-mean offset reflects finite-replicate Monte Carlo variation.
interpretation.standard_error: Estimated spread of the mean over repeated samples of the same size
interpretation.sampling_approximation: Bootstrap distributions approximate the sampling distributions using the observed empirical distribution.
interpretation.normal_reference: Reference curves are centered at the observed mean with SD equal to the analytic SE; they do not assume normal individual measurements.
interpretation.confidence_intervals: Under repeated sampling with the stated assumptions, a nominal 95% procedure covers the target population parameter in about 95% of repeated samples.
interpretation.generalization: The sampling frame and selection probabilities are undocumented. Confidence intervals depend on the sampling assumptions and the stated eligibility rules.
interpretation.limits: Agreement between bootstrap and t intervals in this sample does not establish their population coverage or remove sampling-frame limitations.
